item.text:
**5B.4 — Mixed, leaning no**

Sisi’s 2024 record includes real rule-setting for private investment and competition, especially on FX liberalization, SOE governance, and some land/investment rules. But the same 2024 evidence still shows a state-dominated economy where SOEs and military-linked firms kept major advantages, enforcement remained uneven, and private actors still faced opaque, distorted rules. So this is better described as partial reform than a fair, level playing field.

**Supports**
- **World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts** | World Bank Group | 2024-03-18 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts | The World Bank says Egypt’s program targets private sector growth and job creation, asset monetization, stronger SOE governance, more private sector participation, and reforms to level the playing field. This is direct evidence of rules meant to favor entrepreneurship and investment over rent extraction. | `5B.4`, `5B.1`, `5B.3`
- **IMF Staff and the Egyptian Authorities Reach Staff Level Agreement on the First and Second Reviews under the EFF Arrangement** | IMF | 2024-03-06 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement | The IMF says the reforms included a flexible exchange rate, tighter monetary/fiscal policy, and slower infrastructure spending to preserve debt sustainability while fostering private sector activity. That supports a fairer investment climate and more predictable rules. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **IMF Reaches Staff Level Agreement on the Third Review of the Extended Fund Facility with Egypt** | IMF | 2024-06-06 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/06/pr-24208-egypt-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-3rd-review-of-the-eff | The IMF says the agenda was to raise private-sector-led growth, create fiscal space for health and education, and improve the business environment by reducing the state’s role. That is strong evidence of formal rule changes intended to support competition and job creation. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **Egypt - United States Department of State, 2024 Investment Climate Statements** | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/ | The report says Law 11 of 2024 removed previous sector-specific limits on foreign investors owning land in Sinai, and it notes the National Title Registration Program’s attempt to simplify property registration and cap fees. This is a concrete positive on investment/property-rights rules, though still limited. | `5B.4`
- **Egypt: Creating Jobs by Improving the Regulatory Environment for Investors** | World Bank Group | 2022, cited in 2024 context | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2022/05/12/egypt-creating-jobs-by-improving-the-regulatory-environment-for-investors | World Bank describes major reductions in licensing and land-allocation delays under EASE, showing the type of investor-rule simplification Egypt had been trying to build on. This is older than 2024, but it helps explain the reform direction that 2024 continued. | `5B.4`, `5B.1`

**Cuts against**
- **Egypt - United States Department of State, 2024 Investment Climate Statements** | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/ | The report also says SOEs and military-owned companies enjoy significant advantages, including relief from regulatory requirements and tax exemptions, and that private firms complain about inconsistent enforcement against state and military entities. This is direct evidence that the rules were not yet fair in practice. | `5B.4`
- **Improving the business climate to revive private sector growth: OECD Economic Surveys: Egypt 2024** | OECD | 2024 | https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-egypt-2024_af900de2-en/full-report/component-8.html | OECD says wide-reaching state involvement crowds out the private sector, military-owned firms have tax and land/resource advantages, and ownership/management processes lack transparency. That is strong evidence against fair competition and neutral market rules. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`, `5B.2`
- **Arab Republic of Egypt: First and Second Reviews Under the Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-03-29 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/29/pr24101-egypt-imf-executive-board-completes-first-second-reviews-eff-approves-augmentation | The IMF says Egypt still needed to reduce public investment and withdraw the state and military from economic activity, which means the market was still structurally tilted toward state power. That undercuts any claim that Sisi had already created fair entrepreneurial rules. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`
- **Arab Republic of Egypt: First and Second Reviews Under the Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility, Monetary Policy Consultation...** | IMF staff report | 2024 | https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/098/article-A001-en.xml | The staff report says the state ownership policy applies to military-owned companies and that the government had to reinstate public reporting on the SOE portfolio. That is evidence the state still had to be pushed toward transparency and fairer competition. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`
- **IMF Frequently Asked Questions on Egypt and the IMF** | IMF | 2024 | https://www.imf.org/en/countries/egy/egypt-qandas | The IMF says the private sector still needed stronger competition rules, more transparency, easier land acquisition, trade facilitation, and stronger anti-corruption measures. That reads as unfinished reform, not a fully fair rule set. | `5B.4`, `5B.3`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on SOEs, investment, land, and competition, but not much direct 2024 evidence on day-to-day startup formation, SME treatment, or court enforcement of property rights in individual disputes.
- The biggest unresolved question is implementation: several reforms exist on paper, but there is little independent 2024 proof that military/state-linked firms lost their practical advantages at scale.
